pr_title: Bluetooth: audio: test: Unit tests for the broadcast reception start procedure
pr_body:
This implements the first unittests for the broadcast reception start procedure.
There is some more parameter checking in the broadcast reception start, which are not tested yet. A separate PR will follow for this.


Fixes #68869

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: LE audio: CAP commander: broadcast reception start unittest
issue_context.body:
Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Add a unit test for verification of the implementation mentioned in issue #64358

Describe the solution you'd like
Implement a babblesim test

Describe alternatives you've considered
A unittest is probably too complex for this issue

Additional context
see #64358

review_comments: What does this test that `test_commander_reception_start` doesn't?
Test with one subgroup instead of CONFIG_BT_BAP_BASS_MAX_SUBGROUPS

Right, but what if we modify `CONFIG_BT_BAP_BASS_MAX_SUBGROUPS` to be e.g. `4`?
Would you do tests for 1, 2 and 3 as well? 

If you want to test all possible values, then it should have been a loop over the values, rather than just a single test for a specific count. 

My original point was whether this will actually hit any code that wasn't already covered by a test?

> Right, but what if we modify `CONFIG_BT_BAP_BASS_MAX_SUBGROUPS` to be e.g. `4`? Would you do tests for 1, 2 and 3 as well?
> 
> If you want to test all possible values, then it should have been a loop over the values, rather than just a single test for a specific count.
> 
> My original point was whether this will actually hit any code that wasn't already covered by a test?

We could loop, but I think it is sufficient to test for illegal values (0 and CONFIG_BT_BAP_BASS_MAX_SUBGROUPS+1), maximum, and minimum.

Minor, but it may make more sense to do
```suggestion
	zassert_equal(err, -EINVAL, "Unexpected return value %d", err);
```

Even though the result is the same
I agree, but this makes it inconsistent with `test_micp.c` and `test_vcp.c`
Indeed, and they should probably have been the other way around. For the upcoming CAP initiator tests I'm doing `err, -EINVAL`
I prefer to keep it at least consistent for the CAP commander test, and rather create a separate PR reversing the order if that is what we want
